questions.question: Why can count++ lose updates when two threads run it on the same field?
options: It is really three steps, read, add and write, which can interleave
int fields cannot be shared between threads
The JVM skips every second increment
questions.explanation: Both threads can read the same old value, add one, and write the same result, so one increment disappears.

questions.question: Which lock does a synchronized instance method use?
options: A new lock for every call
The lock of this, the object the method is called on
questions.explanation: A synchronized instance method locks this. A static synchronized method locks the Class object instead.

questions.question: Which lock does static synchronized void addToCity() in class Booth use?
options: A private lock created by the compiler
questions.explanation: Static synchronized methods lock the Class object, so every Booth instance shares the same lock for them.

questions.question: Four threads each call a synchronized add() 500 times on one shared counter, and main joins all four. What does main print for the count?
questions.explanation: The synchronized method makes each increment atomic, and join() waits for every thread, so the total is exactly 4 x 500.

questions.question: Two threads each call their own new Counter().inc(), where inc() is synchronized and adds to a static int. Why is the static total still wrong?
options: Each thread locks a different Counter object, so they do not exclude each other
questions.explanation: An instance lock protects only that object. Shared static data needs a static synchronized method or one shared lock object.

questions.question: A field is declared volatile int sold; and several threads run sold++. What is still wrong?
options: volatile gives visibility but not atomicity, so updates can still be lost
questions.explanation: volatile makes reads see the latest write, but read, add and write can still interleave. Use synchronized or AtomicInteger.

questions.question: What state is a thread in while it waits to enter a synchronized block that another thread holds?
questions.explanation: A thread waiting for a monitor lock is BLOCKED until the owner releases it.

questions.question: A thread already holds the lock on an object and calls another synchronized method on that same object. What happens?
options: It enters at once, because intrinsic locks are reentrant
questions.explanation: Java monitors are reentrant. The owning thread can enter any code guarded by the same lock without waiting.

questions.question: A method does if (seats > 0) { seats--; } with only the seats-- line inside synchronized. Why can seats still go below zero?
options: The check runs outside the lock, so two threads can both pass it before either decrements
The if statement is ignored by the JVM
questions.explanation: Check-then-act must be atomic as a whole. Put the check and the change in the same synchronized block.

questions.question: A synchronized method runs throw new RuntimeException() halfway through. What happens to the lock?
options: It is released automatically as the exception leaves the method
questions.explanation: The JVM releases an intrinsic lock whenever the synchronized code exits, whether it returns normally or throws.
